The local networking group, Ladies Out Lunching – LOL for short – will host their July Luncheon at Lost Pizza Company in Benton, Wednesday, August 19th from 12:00 – 1:00 pm. 

Come ready to chat and make some new friends! 

Luncheon Details:

– Lunch is Dutch Treat: just order and pay your meal.

– Don’t forget to bring your business cards and materials!

– Happy Gift: If you would like a minute to share about your business bring a small gift or some business swag to share! We will draw for a recipient and you get a chance to share – everyone loves a present… right?

NONPROFIT SUPPORT! This month we are collecting nonperishable food items and feminine hygiene products for local food pantries.

LOL meets the 3rd Wednesday of each month at various restaurants around Saline County.  Learn more about LOL and RSVP to an event by visiting  www.facebook.com/groups/ladiesoutlunching/

item.title: Entergy suspends disconnects through August 21 amid extreme heat wave
item.dc:creator: Shelli Poole
item.description: Entergy Arkansas has announced a temporary suspension of residential service disconnections for all customers through Friday, August 21, to protect public safety during a period of extreme heat. The utility provider confirmed that disconnection procedures will not resume until Monday, August 24, as dangerous temperatures continue to impact communities across the state. Read more below. […]
item.content:encoded:
Entergy Arkansas has announced a temporary suspension of residential service disconnections for all customers through Friday, August 21, to protect public safety during a period of extreme heat. The utility provider confirmed that disconnection procedures will not resume until Monday, August 24, as dangerous temperatures continue to impact communities across the state. Read more below.




The temporary suspension is a proactive safety measure intended to help residents keep their cooling systems running during the ongoing heat wave. Company officials noted that while they are pausing disconnections, this does not prevent the possibility of unexpected power outages caused by severe weather, emergencies, or equipment damage.

In addition to suspending shutoffs, Entergy Arkansas has issued a set of critical guidelines to help customers manage their energy usage and avoid heat-related health emergencies. Cooling costs typically represent the largest portion of a household’s electric bill during the summer, but several low-cost or no-cost strategies can significantly reduce energy consumption:

  • Adjust the thermostat:
    Residents are advised to set their thermostats to the highest temperature that remains comfortable.
  • Maintain air-conditioning units:
    Routinely cleaning or replacing air filters helps systems run more efficiently.
  • Utilize fans:
    Ceiling and portable fans can effectively circulate cool air, though they should be turned off when rooms are unoccupied.
  • Block sunlight:
    Closing blinds, curtains, and shades during the hottest afternoon hours helps keep indoor temperatures down.
  • Seal air leaks:
    Gaps around doors, windows, and ductwork should be sealed to keep conditioned air from escaping.

Entergy Arkansas offers energy-monitoring resources through its online portal, where customers can use myAdvisor tools to track real-time energy use and identify custom savings options. Additional energy-efficiency programs, rebates, and bill-assistance tools are available through the company’s online Bill Toolkit.

For those working outdoors, safety remains paramount. Health experts advise drinking plenty of water, scheduling strenuous labor during the coolest times of the day, and taking frequent breaks in shaded or air-conditioned areas. Signs of heat exhaustion include heavy sweating, headache, nausea, and extreme fatigue. If an individual shows signs of heat stroke—such as confusion, seizures, hot and dry skin, or loss of consciousness—emergency services should be contacted immediately.

For additional energy-saving, bill-management and customer assistance resources, visit Entergy Arkansas.

item.title: Saline County to host ‘Carry the Light’ vigil for first responder suicide prevention on September 1
item.dc:creator: Shelli Poole
item.description: Community members, first responders, and local leaders will gather on the Saline County Courthouse lawn next month for “Carry the Light,” an event dedicated to first responder suicide prevention and remembrance. Scheduled for Tuesday, Sept. 1, 2026, the evening aims to honor those lost, support those currently struggling, and foster a supportive community where seeking […]
item.content:encoded:
Community members, first responders, and local leaders will gather on the Saline County Courthouse lawn next month for “Carry the Light,” an event dedicated to first responder suicide prevention and remembrance. Scheduled for Tuesday, Sept. 1, 2026, the evening aims to honor those lost, support those currently struggling, and foster a supportive community where seeking help is viewed as a sign of strength. Read more below.




The gathering, which begins at 6:30 p.m., will formally recognize Sept. 1 as First Responder Suicide Prevention Day. The program will include the presentation of official proclamations recognizing the day at both the state and county levels.

For event organizer Serena Krone, the date carries a deeply personal significance. Her sister, Brittany Wildhaber, a volunteer firefighter and EMT, died by suicide on Sept. 1, 2017.

“For nine years, September 1 has represented one of the darkest days of my life,” Krone said. “I can’t change what happened that day, but I can help change what this day means going forward. My hope is that September 1 becomes a day when we remember those we’ve lost while reminding the first responders who are still here that they matter, they are needed, and they never have to carry the weight of this job alone.”

A central portion of the evening will be the symbolic “Carry the Light” candle observance. Attendees will carry candles representing both remembrance and hope, honoring the departed while showing solidarity with active first responders who face unseen struggles.

“Sometimes someone can’t see the light for themselves,” Krone noted. “In those moments, we have to be willing to carry it for them until they can see it again.”

The event is open to the public and is designed to bring together firefighters, EMS professionals, law enforcement officers, dispatchers, their families, elected officials, and the broader Saline County community. Organizers emphasize that the public’s presence serves as a powerful demonstration of support for the men and women who spend their lives responding to emergencies.

The upcoming community event features two separate flights, meals for participants, and various prize opportunities. Read more below. The tournament will host two scheduled flights for teams. Morning […]
item.content:encoded:
The Saline Home Builders Association is preparing to host its 2026 “Fore the Builders” Golf Tournament on Thursday, Sept. 17, at the Hurricane Golf & Country Club.

The upcoming community event features two separate flights, meals for participants, and various prize opportunities. Read more below.




The tournament will host two scheduled flights for teams. Morning participants can check in and enjoy breakfast during the 8 a.m. registration period, with the first flight officially teeing off at 8:30 a.m.

Afternoon players will have a separate registration and lunch starting at noon, followed by the second flight at 1 p.m.

The team entry fee is set at $450. Additionally, attendees can purchase a separate game package for $60. The tournament will conclude with the distribution of prizes and awards to the participating golfers.

Those interested in registering a team or seeking further information about the event can contact Amy with the Saline Home Builders Association by calling 501-909-8055 or emailing salinehba@gmail.com.

item.title: Police narrative reveals murder victim from Saline County recorded his own death on cell phone
item.dc:creator: Shelli Poole
item.description: UPDATE AUG 12, 2026 EARLIER: JUL 15, 2026 Chilling details have emerged in the capital murder case with suspects Yudith Cicard Reyes and Luis Felipe Reyes-Isabel of Saline County, Arkansas. Court records reveal that the victim, Jose Miguel Quiroz-Mata, recorded his own fatal shooting on his cell phone. Read more below. Quiroz-Mata, age 44, was […]
item.content:encoded:
UPDATE AUG 12, 2026
EARLIER: JUL 15, 2026

Chilling details have emerged in the capital murder case with suspects Yudith Cicard Reyes and Luis Felipe Reyes-Isabel of Saline County, Arkansas. Court records reveal that the victim, Jose Miguel Quiroz-Mata, recorded his own fatal shooting on his cell phone. Read more below.




Quiroz-Mata, age 44, was found dead inside his vehicle in Little Rock on July 14, 2026, just days after he had repeatedly contacted law enforcement to report a suspected arson, escalating threats, and the physical sabotage of his vehicle.

According to an arrest affidavit from the Little Rock Police Department, officers responded to a ShotSpotter alert and subsequent shooting call at approximately 6:09 a.m. on July 14, 2026, in the 4200 block of W. 10th St.

Upon arrival, first responders located Quiroz-Mata deceased in the driver’s seat of his white Chevrolet, suffering from multiple gunshot wounds. Processing of the crime scene yielded three .380-caliber cartridge casings, shattered glass, and a projectile strike on the driver’s side door frame.

Yudith Cicard Reyes • Arrest Date: 07/14/2026 • Agency: Little Rock Police Department • Age: 49 • White Female • DOB: 05/06/1977 • Charged with: #1 warrant: affidavit-felony warrant issued by little rock police department, ar; #2 CAPITAL MURDER • NO BOND.
Luis Reyes • Arrest Date: 07/14/2026 • Agency: Little Rock Police Department • Age:22 • White Male • DOB: 10/20/2003 • Charged with: #1 warrant: affidavit-felony warrant issued by ar. NO BOND, ICE PENDING.


The breakthrough in the investigation came when detectives discovered Quiroz-Mata’s cell phone on the driver-side floorboard of his vehicle. After obtaining the passcode from family members, detectives discovered a video recording captured by the victim immediately prior to his death.

The footage captured a black truck blocking the roadway, followed by a male identified as 22-year-old Luis Felipe Reyes-Isabel approaching the victim’s vehicle with a handgun and firing five rounds inside.

Witnesses in the neighborhood reported hearing five gunshots, seeing a black truck follow a white truck, and hearing screams. One witness told detectives they specifically observed Quiroz-Mata’s ex-wife, 49-year-old Yudith Reyes, sitting in the front passenger seat of the suspect vehicle during the shooting.

Additionally, a resident’s security camera captured footage of Quiroz-Mata’s white Chevy striking a mailbox at 6:08 a.m., with the black truck trailing slowly behind it.

Using Flock license plate readers, investigators tracked the movements of a black 2026 Dodge Ram registered to Yudith Reyes. The vehicle was recorded northbound on Chicot Road at 3:30 a.m. and southbound on Cedar Street at 3:51 a.m. City surveillance cameras also captured both Yudith Reyes and Reyes-Isabel riding in the truck together on Geyer Springs Road at 6:18 a.m., minutes after the shooting.

Later that morning, detectives spotted Yudith Reyes’s second vehicle, a Chevrolet Trailblazer, at an office strip at the 10600 of Colonel Glenn Road, and took her into custody without incident.

Investigators subsequently executed a search-and-seizure warrant at her home located in the Royal Oaks neighborhood in Mabelvale. Inside the residence, police recovered a Ruger .380-caliber gun box, a paycheck stub for Reyes-Isabel, and his state fisheries conservation license.

After being read her Miranda rights, Yudith Reyes provided a recorded statement admitting that Reyes-Isabel drove the truck to the crime scene, shot Quiroz-Mata, and fled.

Although she initially claimed Reyes-Isabel was her cousin, family members refuted that assertion to police. Both suspects are currently being held without bond at the Pulaski County Regional Jail on charges of capital murder. Mr. Reyes-Isabel has a case pending with Immigration & Customs Enforcement (ICE).

The arrest affidavit also reveals that Mr. Quiroz-Mata had spent weeks pleading with authorities for assistance as the situation escalated. On June 15, 2026, he reported to police that his ex-wife may have been responsible for a house fire.

On July 9, he filed a formal harassment complaint at the prosecuting attorney’s office. Finally, on July 12 — just 48 hours before he was killed — Quiroz-Mata filed a police report stating that Reyes’s boyfriend had physically sabotaged his vehicle.

item.content:encoded:
Habitat for Humanity will present their second annual Murder Mystery Dinner Theater. This fun fundraiser will have dinner and a show, along with pre-show hors d’oevres. There will also be a silent and live auction, and casino games.




Sponsored by Ridout Lumber Company and Saline County Home Builders Association, the event is set for Thursday, October 15th at the Hill Barn Event Center on 100 Hill Road in Bryant. That’s off Reynolds Road and adjacent to Hill Barn Elementary School.

Doors open at 6PM, dinner and show begins at 7PM and the auctions and casino games continue the evening at 8PM.

Watch for information on tickets and more at https://habitatsalinecounty.com/.
